messages.subject: Installing rstan with bleeding-edge stanlib
parts:
Hi - 

I was just wondering if there was a straightforward way to install rstan with the newest development version of Stan from github. I see that the main stan repo is downloaded when you clone the rstan repo and I was wondering if there was a simple way to change that hook to the newest version (or if it would be possible to add one like that to the rstan repo).

Thanks!

-Jon

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Installing rstan with bleeding-edge stanlib
parts: On Wed, Mar 5, 2014 at 4:00 PM, Jon Zelner <jze...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi - 

I was just wondering if there was a straightforward way to install rstan with the newest development version of Stan from github.

Not at the moment. We are currently refactoring Stan, CmdStan, and RStan simultaneously. You're not going to be able to do it easily from the develop branch of RStan.

There is, however, a branch I'm working on that is experimental and is up to date with the current version of Stan. It's feature/refactor_stan_command.

I see that the main stan repo is downloaded when you clone the rstan repo and I was wondering if there was a simple way to change that hook to the newest version (or if it would be possible to add one like that to the rstan repo).

That isn't true. Stan is a submodule inside RStan. It does not get downloaded automatically.

There are easy ways to change the submodule version. Read up on git submodules to find out how to use them. (They're tricky, but not impossible and it's beyond the scope of our users list to discuss how to use git.)
 

Thanks!

Good luck! If you end up being able to do it easily, please write it down and let us know.

-Jon
